rows.grounds: compound; result of that hearing/qualification mentioned previously
compound; gone to the hand, i.e. immediately accessible
compound; one who stands at the door/gate, guardian of access
used adverbially in context; even in hidden or esoteric matters

items.question: Why is the fruit of that hearing immediately accessible to the qualified recipient?
premises: The fruit of that hearing is in the recipient's hand.
The recipient is always the keeper of the door.
This role of door-keeper holds even in secret matters.
items.inference: Because the qualified recipient constantly guards access, including in secret contexts, the fruit of that hearing is immediately within reach.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tat+phalaṃ depends on the preceding verse's tat+śrutau.
rahasya is taken adverbially as in-secret though its surface form is neuter nominative singular.
items.plain_english: Indeed, that fruit is in your hand, because you are always the doorkeeper, even in secret.
